summary: Iteration 6: weekly scorecards, history isolation, load-order labels, customer rating, booking sms_status. New suite test_scorecard_rating_labels.py passes 14/14. Regression: 43/44 pass (excluding the paid test_twilio_contact.py). Two old asserts were updated for the intended nice_date alert format. The one remaining failure is a time-dependent optimizer test, not a regression. Frontend: the driver summary THIS WEEK scorecard has 7 bars and 7 rows, and its totals match the rows. Admin DRIVER SCORECARDS are sorted best on-time first, and tapping one opens /driver/summary/drv-2. Delivering with a signature, then 4 stars + FRIENDLY DRIVER on the customer screen, shows rating-thanks and the toast, and survives a reload. The rating is persisted (rating=4, comment='FRIENDLY DRIVER') and shows in the summary avg_rating 4.0. The customer window booking toast still works. No real SMS or calls were sent: all numbers were fictional and returned skipped_fictional. Data was reset at the end. Deprecated packages detected: none.

minor.issue: The sort key -(on_time_rate or -1) treats a 0% on-time rate the same as no windowed data (None), so they tie.
rated_at is set on every history stop, including unrated and failed ones. It should only be set when rating is set.
days_worked counts today as soon as a route is started (drv-1 shows '7 DAYS WORKED' with today at 0 drops). Acceptable, but worth knowing.

Performance: for each driver, each day and each route it makes separate get_stops calls (about 21+ DB round trips plus per-route queries). Fine for the demo, but should be aggregated if there are many drivers.

issues: Once the order is delivered, the map area is an empty grid with only the YOU marker hidden behind the banner. Consider shrinking the map or centring on the drop pin.

action_items: Optional: fix the /scorecards sort so 0% on-time ranks above drivers with no data (use `x['on_time_rate'] if x['on_time_rate'] is not None else -1`).
Optional: in seed_history, only set rated_at when a rating exists.

Optional: make tests/test_qr_windows.py::test_optimize_moves_urgent_stop_earlier tolerant of the depot-to-first-stop ETA. It sets window end = now+12 min, but the ETA to the first drop can be later than that, so late_stops stays 1 even though the stop correctly moves to seq 1.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1272 lines (over 700). Split it into routers (scorecards/analytics, stops, routes, twilio, labels).
day_stats 'on_time' counts deliveries without a window as on time, while on_time_rate counts only windowed deliveries. The two fields mean different things.
The rating endpoint has no auth or ownership check: anyone with a stop id can rate once. This matches the app's no-auth design.
RatingPrompt sends only the selected tags as the comment; there is no free-text field.
